Use-case & requirements (concise):
- Workloads: mix of streaming chat (progressive token streaming into UI) and non-streaming short completions for reranking.
- Targets requested (starting point): non-streaming: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms, p99 < 500ms (end-to-end e2e as measured from client SDK). Streaming: per-chunk latency p95 < 100ms; final-turn p99 < 700ms.
- Throughput: steady-state 2k qps across 10 regions with spikes to 6k qps (burst reserve needed). Average tokens per request ~18 tokens.
- Cost: high sensitivity; want quantization & batching recommendations to hit cost target while preserving latency.

Key measurement alignment items discussed / open:
- Client-side vs server-side timing: Peregrine insists SLOs are e2e (client-observed). Redwood proposals include server-side metrics (enqueue, start-of-first-token, last-token) + an agreed client instrumentation shim for SDK to capture network+TLS + app-side overhead.
- Definition artifacts to finalize: 
  * Non-streaming latency: measured from SDK request timestamp (after request body written) to SDK receipt of final token. Include TCP/TLS handshake only for cold connections; baseline uses keep-alive connections.
  * Streaming latency: two signals — per-chunk first-byte latency (for UI progressive rendering) and overall time-to-last-byte. SLOs to be defined per-signal.
  * p50/p95/p99: percentiles computed on the same aggregation window (1h) and on rolling 24h for SLA evaluation. Need agreement on exclusion list for maintenance windows and planned capacity changes.
  * Cold-start definition: any request served by a new container instance (no warmed KV cache) — separate metric bucket; negotiations on whether cold-starts count toward SLA.
- Tracing & instrumentation: require propagated trace_id through SDK -> load-balancer -> inference runtime. Redwood to provide OpenTelemetry-compatible spans + example SDK instrumentation. Peregrine will add client-side SDK timers and correlate with trace_id.
- Sampling & stats: recommend 100% server-side metrics for infra; client-side sample rate 10% for full traces, 100% for lightweight timing telemetry.

Throughput & reserved GPU planning notes:
- Initial reserved capacity ask: 20 A100-equivalent GPUs in 3 shards (regionally distributed) with 20% burst headroom. Redwood to propose shard sizing based on measured tokens/sec and average seq length.
- Autoscaling policy: prefer scheduled scaling + burst queueing with graceful degradation to lower-capacity quantized variants. Peregrine requires explicit RU (reserved units) that map to guaranteed throughput.
- Load profile specifics: baseline 2k rps, P99 request size 90th pct tokens ~40 tokens; target sustained tokens/sec estimate ~36k tps. Redwood to translate to GPU RPS and concurrency.

SLA & negotiation topics:
- Credit model: Peregrine wants credits for each calendar month on p99 misses beyond agreed threshold. Legal wants formula with cap (e.g., max 20% of monthly recurring fee).
- Maintenance windows: Peregrine requires <1 hour planned monthly downtime or scheduled windows outside market hours.
